summary: Wave 3 AI features (voice-to-rx, patient-gist, lab-ocr) + Wave 1 /api/search link regression — all 18/18 tests PASS. Auth gating verified (401 without token, 403 for demo accounts, 403 for non-prescriber on voice-to-rx). Empty/oversized/bad-MIME inputs return 400 as designed. Response shapes match contract (ok, model='claude-sonnet-4-5', stt_model='whisper-1', parsed.medicines[] etc.). Patient-gist cache layer works: first call cached=false, second within an hour cached=true with identical gist, refresh=true bypasses. Lab-ocr graceful-degrades on synthetic 1×1 PNG (empty results, saved_count=0). Search regression confirmed: disease links use singular /disease/{id}, blog links use /blog/{post_id} (verified via seeded TEST_ blog), calculators are nested under /calculators/{key} except /ipss and /prostate-volume which stay top-level. Found and fixed ONE real bug in wave3.py patient_gist cache read (offset-naive vs offset-aware datetime comparison crashed second-call lookup with 500).

minor.issue: FIXED in this iteration — cached read raised TypeError comparing offset-naive (Mongo-returned) vs offset-aware (now) datetimes. Re-attached UTC tzinfo on read. See updated_files.

action_items: Optional: in /app/backend/routers/wave3.py also normalise generated_at tzinfo when persisting — currently cached docs are written with tz-aware datetimes but Mongo strips tz, so any other consumer (frontend, audit) reading patient_gist_cache directly will need the same .replace(tzinfo=utc) treatment. Consider a helper _to_aware_utc() shared across wave routers.
Consider extracting /api/search into its own router — wave1.py is now 818 lines and search logic spans ~340 lines.
Consider adding an explicit ref_range field validator in lab-ocr response — currently a free-form string from Claude.
critical_code_review_comments: wave3.py patient_gist had a latent crash on every second (cached) call due to datetime tz mismatch — only surfaced under back-to-back same-phone calls within the 1h window. Fixed.

voice-to-rx writes the upload to /tmp/v2rx_*.{ext} and unlinks in finally — good. But there's no size cap *before* read() — the 25 MB check happens only after the bytes are already in memory. Consider Content-Length pre-check for robustness.
lab-ocr accepts WebP per MIME sniff (RIFF header) but the request must still be ≤8 MB — that limit is also post-read; same pre-check suggestion.

patient_gist context query for bookings/prescriptions uses suffix-regex on patient_phone (unanchored start) — this works because _normalize_phone returns the last 10 digits, but a malicious phone like '8888888888' could collide with another patient sharing the same trailing 10. In practice fine since _normalize_phone enforces 10-digit canonicalisation everywhere.

rca_of_issue: patient_gist 500 RCA: motor/pymongo deserialises BSON datetimes as Python `datetime` instances WITHOUT tzinfo (default behaviour). The handler stored `expires_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc) + 1h` (aware) but compared the *read-back* naive value against `now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)` (aware) → `TypeError: can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware datetimes`. Fix: on read, if `expires_at.tzinfo is None`, re-attach `tzinfo=timezone.utc` before the comparison; same treatment applied to `generated_at` in the response payload. Alternative durable fix would be configuring motor with `tz_aware=True` at client creation, which would benefit every consumer of this DB. Reproduction: call /api/ai/patient-gist twice in succession with the same phone — first 200 (writes cache), second 500. Mitigation deployed in this iteration.
